summary.short: Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information regulates how personal information business operators, pseudonymized and anonymized information handlers and administrative organs handle personal data. It sets purpose limits, security, third-party and cross-border transfer rules, individual rights, and criminal penalties, and creates the Personal Information Protection Commission.
summary.long: The Act defines personal information and related categories (pseudonymously processed, anonymously processed and personal-related information) and sets basic principles and duties of the national and local governments, including a cabinet-approved basic policy. Chapter 4 imposes duties on personal information handling business operators: purpose specification and use limits, proper acquisition, notice of purposes, accuracy, security measures, supervision of employees and contractors, breach reporting, limits on third-party provision and transfers to foreign third parties, record-keeping, and rules for pseudonymized and anonymized information; accredited protection organizations are also provided for. Chapter 5 applies parallel duties to administrative organs, including registration of personal information files and rights to request disclosure, correction and suspension of use. Chapter 6 establishes the Personal Information Protection Commission, empowered to give guidance, require reports, inspect premises, and issue recommendations and orders. Chapter 8 sets criminal penalties, including up to one year's imprisonment or a 1 million yen fine for violating a Commission order, and corporate fines up to 100 million yen for certain violations. Article 171 extends the Act to foreign handling connected with goods or services offered to persons in Japan. The text includes supplementary provisions from Act No. 37 of 2021, whose provisions take effect on dates set out in that Act, including 1 September 2021.
